Standing priorities are to maintain discipline during forced inactivity while awaiting the resolution wave cluster to clear and to perform a comprehensive fresh scan rather than acting on stale watchlist items.

decisions.question: Will the percent of Pakistanis in extreme poverty be above 5 percent in 2023?
decisions.thinking: Given the 2018 baseline was already 4.93%, even a minimal net disruption from the 2022 floods and inflation crisis pushes the headcount rate above 5.0%.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether official survey-based consumption tabulations published via World Bank/OWID reflect the flood/inflation impact or smooth it via modeled estimates.
decisions.resolution_risk: Data revision differences or shifting definitions between the $1.90 and $2.15 poverty line benchmarks.
evidence_for: Baseline extreme poverty in Pakistan was already 4.93% in 2018, leaving a tiny margin (0.08 percentage points) to exceed 5.0%.
The 2022 catastrophic floods and subsequent 2022-2023 macroeconomic crisis and high inflation caused major shocks to low-income households.
World Bank simulations estimated that the 2022 floods alone pushed millions of additional people into poverty.
evidence_against: Targeted social safety net expansions like the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) mitigated extreme consumption shocks.
World Bank model projections from early 2023 suggested potential modest long-term declines if post-Covid recovery outpaced shocks.
